result: {"self_assessment": "Impact: I kept the table supplied for the whole build. I made four full 40-domino runs to the shared bin, at 0:45, 2:00, 3:00 and 4:00, so the builders never stopped for material. The table ended with a connected 143-domino fish outline that falls from the start domino. Execution: After the supply runs I moved to inspecting and repairing. I inspected the lower tail fork several times, stood dominoes back up, laid 5 more to carry the fork past its end and curl it up round the tail, and nudged the off-line domino near the tip. The inspections after that showed the whole run connected through to the end of the fork. Collaboration: I told the table what I was fetching and what I was fixing, so we avoided overlapping work. When Priya and Tom flagged the break near the tip, I confirmed the nudge was already done, and we all agreed to keep hands off before the push. I also pointed out a small break in the upper lobe to Maya. Leadership: I took ownership of the supply role without being asked twice and moved to the lower fork when it needed an owner. I helped steer the table towards hands off once the run was connected, which cut the risk of a late bump. I think my share of the result was about 30 percent, mainly the steady supply and the fork repair work.", "my_share_percent": 30}
